start_here: Say to your AI: "Write the files of a repository, the dates of its commits and a stamp naming the commit into my own files under /source-copies/<root>/, so a check of what a finding cites can read them on any computer", with {"root":"sample-repo","ref":"origin/main","head":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","files":[{"path":"src/a.txt","text":"first line\nsecond line\n"}],"dates":{"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567":"2026-11-10T10:00:00Z"},"complete":true}. It runs tool:write-a-source-copy and answers {"root":"sample-repo","head":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567","written":1,"bytes":238}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows () through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Write the files of a repository, the dates of its commits and a stamp naming the commit into my own files under /source-copies/<root>/, so a check of what a finding cites can read them on any computer", and give it root (The name of the copy folder under /source-copies/ (the root name a resolver lists)); ref (The ref the copy was made from); head (The commit the copy was made from); files (The files to write, at their repository paths); dates (Full commit hash to ISO date).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:write-a-source-copy and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Takes a root name, the ref and head the copy was made from, a list of files ({path, text}, at most 64, each at most 4 MiB), the commit dates ({<full hash>: <ISO date>}) and whether the list is every tracked file.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: undefined (find_file, read_file, write_file_start, write_file_piece, write_file_finish).
